question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European trading settlements in India before the First Carnatic War]
options: French East India Company — Pondicherry (headquarters on the Coromandel Coast)
English East India Company — Madras (Fort St. George on the Coromandel Coast)
Dutch East India Company — Nagapattinam (major base on the Coromandel Coast)
Portuguese — Surat (principal headquarters of their Indian trade)
wrong_fact: Portuguese headquarters in India was Goa, not Surat. Surat was the main base of the English East India Company in western India in the early 17th century.
explanation: Before the First Carnatic War (1746–48), European powers had established key footholds: the French at Pondicherry, the English at Madras (Fort St. George), and the Dutch at Nagapattinam — all on the Coromandel Coast. The Portuguese, the earliest European power in India, had their principal Indian headquarters at Goa on the western coast, not Surat.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Causes/background of the First Carnatic War — geographic and political context]
options: War of Austrian Succession in Europe — triggered Anglo-French hostilities that spilled into India
Carnatic region — roughly corresponding to the eastern coastal plains under the Nawab of Arcot
Hyderabad — seat of the Nizam-ul-Mulk, nominal overlord of the Carnatic
Diu — the island fortress where the French assembled their fleet before attacking Madras in 1746
wrong_fact: The French fleet under La Bourdonnais sailed from Mauritius (Île de France), not from Diu. Diu is a Portuguese enclave on the Gujarat coast with no role in this conflict.
explanation: The First Carnatic War was the Indian theatre of the War of Austrian Succession (1740–48). The Carnatic was the coastal plain broadly around Madras, nominally under the Nizam of Hyderabad. The French fleet that attacked Madras in 1746 was dispatched from Mauritius (Île de France) by Governor La Bourdonnais — not from Diu, which was a Portuguese-held island in Gujarat entirely unrelated to this conflict.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European territorial possessions and strategic geography in South India, c. 1740]
options: Karikal — French settlement south of Pondicherry on the Coromandel Coast
Masulipatnam — Dutch and later English settlement on the northern Coromandel Coast
Tranquebar (Tharangambadi) — Danish settlement on the Coromandel Coast
Calicut — primary French base on the Malabar Coast used to threaten British Madras
wrong_fact: Calicut (Kozhikode) was not a French base; the French base on the Malabar Coast was Mahé. Calicut was historically associated with the Portuguese and later British trade.
explanation: By the 1740s, the Coromandel Coast had multiple European enclaves: Karikal (French, south of Pondicherry), Masulipatnam (an English factory, earlier Dutch), and Tranquebar (Danish, established 1620). The French Malabar Coast settlement was Mahé (captured 1725), not Calicut. Calicut was where Vasco da Gama first landed and it later became an important British commercial town, not a French base.
